lessonRef.unitTitle: PF7 — Paying Taxes: Taxes, Take-Home Pay, and Your First Forms
lessonRef.title: Error and misconception analysis: federal, state, and local taxes a person is likely to pay

focus: federal, state, and local taxes a person is likely to pay
objective: Find the error in a fictional claim that a refund means no tax was paid, compute what was actually paid, and state what a refund does and does not measure.
scenario: A fictional filer wrote: "I got a $2,100 refund, so I did not really pay any tax this year." The simulated figures behind that refund are given below.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional filing summary in these directions

tasks.directions: The fictional filing summary: total withheld across the year $6,480, total tax owed for the year $4,380.

prompts.text: What refund do those two figures produce?
How much tax did this filer actually pay for the year?

tasks.directions: Test the filer’s reasoning against a second fictional case with the same income and the same tax owed but different withholding of $4,100.

prompts.text: In the second case, what is owed at filing?
Which filer paid more tax for the year?
choices: The first, who got a refund
The second, who owed at filing
They paid the same amount of tax

prompts.text: What did the fictional filer’s reasoning confuse?
choices: The tax rate with the tax owed
The refund with the tax paid
Nothing; a refund does mean no tax was paid

prompts.text: By how much did the filer understate the tax they paid?
Explain what a refund measures, and describe how you would check whether your own withholding is set sensibly — without using any real figures, describe the two numbers you would compare.

remediation: If the two cases seem to involve different amounts of tax, put the $4,380 figure at the top of both columns. Everything else on the page describes when the money moved, not how much tax there was.
extension: Construct a third fictional case with the same $4,380 owed that produces neither a refund nor a bill, and state what withholding it requires.
